Composite structures are widely used in aerospace engineering, wind energy industry, ship engineering, and civil buildings.
Impact may occur during manufacture, service, and maintenance of composite structures, causing barely visible impact damage.
Impact monitoring is of great importance to ensure the structural health of composite structures.
Wireless sensor network (WSN) offers numerous advantages over conventional wired systems, including low weight and cost, scalability, flexibility, and ease of deployment.
A novel multi-response based global impact localization method is proposed to locate impact occurring sub-regions.
The proposed system has been evaluated on a composite wing and an aircraft composite wing box.
The multi-radio sink node can receive impact localization results from multiple nodes and deliver them to the monitoring center.
The proposed system uses a LabVIEW platform based integrated software as the user interface in the monitoring center.
The clear channel assessment (CCA) mechanism is used to ensure the communication reliability.
The acknowledgement (ACK) mechanism is used to ensure the communication reliability.
The automatic repeat request (ARQ) mechanism is used to ensure the communication reliability.
The proposed system has a high data throughput of 1020Kbps.
